highlight: The standard anatomical position: body erect, face forward, arms at sides with palms facing FORWARD (supinated), feet together pointing forward.
mnemonic: 🧠 'FFFS' — Face Forward, Feet together, Supinated palms

highlight:
3 major planes:
• Sagittal — divides Left & Right
• Coronal (Frontal) — divides Anterior & Posterior
• Transverse (Horizontal) — divides Superior & Inferior
mnemonic: 🧠 'SCT' = Sagittal Cuts Things (Left/Right), Coronal Creates Front/Back, Transverse = Top/Bottom

highlight:
Key pairs:
• Medial / Lateral (toward / away from midline)
• Proximal / Distal (toward / away from origin)
• Superficial / Deep
• Ipsilateral / Contralateral (same / opposite side)
mnemonic: 🧠 'MPSD' — Medial-lateral, Proximal-distal, Superficial-deep

highlight:
Skin = Epidermis + Dermis
• Epidermis: avascular, 5 layers (Stratum Basale → Corneum)
• Dermis: vascular, contains hair follicles, sweat glands, sebaceous glands
• Below dermis = Hypodermis (subcutaneous fat — NOT part of skin)
mnemonic: 🧠 'Come Let's Get Some Beer' = Corneum, Lucidum, Granulosum, Spinosum, Basale

highlight: Langer's lines (cleavage lines) = lines of skin tension running parallel to collagen fiber orientation. Surgical incisions parallel to Langer's lines heal with MINIMAL scarring.
mnemonic: 🧠 'Langer = Less scar' — Cut parallel to Langer's for best healing

highlight:
Two types:
• Superficial fascia (hypodermis): fat + loose CT, contains cutaneous nerves & vessels
• Deep fascia: dense CT, encloses muscles, forms compartments, sheaths, retinacula
mnemonic: 🧠 'Superficial = Soft & fatty, Deep = Dense & tough'

highlight:
5 bone types by shape:
• Long (femur), Short (carpals), Flat (skull), Irregular (vertebrae), Sesamoid (patella)
Bone = compact (cortical) + cancellous (trabecular/spongy)
mnemonic: 🧠 'LFIS+S' = Long, Flat, Irregular, Short + Sesamoid

highlight:
Two types:
• Endochondral ossification: bone replaces cartilage model (long bones, most of skeleton)
• Intramembranous ossification: bone forms directly in connective tissue (flat bones of skull, clavicle)
mnemonic: 🧠 'Endo = inside cartilage, Intramembranous = in membrane (flat bones of skull & clavicle)'

highlight:
3 types:
• Hyaline: articular surfaces, costal cartilages, respiratory tract (most common)
• Elastic: ear, epiglottis, larynx
• Fibrocartilage: intervertebral discs, pubic symphysis, menisci (most compression resistant)
mnemonic: 🧠 'HEF' = Hyaline (Highly common), Elastic (Ears), Fibro (Fibrous discs)

highlight:
By structure:
• Fibrous (sutures, syndesmosis, gomphosis)
• Cartilaginous (synchondrosis = hyaline; symphysis = fibrocartilage)
• Synovial (most common, freely movable)
Synovial joint features: articular cartilage, joint cavity, synovial membrane, capsule
mnemonic: 🧠 'FCS' = Fibrous-Cartilaginous-Synovial (least to most mobile)

highlight:
6 types of synovial joints:
• Plane (intercarpal)
• Hinge (elbow, ankle)
• Pivot (atlantoaxial, radioulnar)
• Condyloid (wrist, MCP)
• Saddle (1st CMC — thumb)
• Ball & Socket (hip, shoulder — most mobile)
mnemonic: 🧠 'Planes Have Pivots Causing Sore Balls' = Plane, Hinge, Pivot, Condyloid, Saddle, Ball & socket

highlight:
3 muscle types:
• Skeletal (striated, voluntary)
• Cardiac (striated, involuntary, intercalated discs)
• Smooth (non-striated, involuntary)
Skeletal muscle: epimysium → perimysium → endomysium
mnemonic: 🧠 'Every Person Eats' = Epimysium, Perimysium, Endomysium (outer to inner)

highlight:
• Origin: proximal/fixed attachment
• Insertion: distal/mobile attachment
• Tendon: muscle to bone (dense regular CT)
• Aponeurosis: flat sheet-like tendon
• Raphe: interdigitating tendons between two muscles
mnemonic: 🧠 'Origin is Old/fixed, Insertion is It that moves'

highlight:
CNS = Brain + Spinal cord
PNS = All nerves outside CNS
PNS divides into:
• Somatic NS (voluntary, skeletal muscle)
• Autonomic NS (involuntary, viscera)
ANS = Sympathetic + Parasympathetic
mnemonic: 🧠 'CNS = Command Center, PNS = Peripheral workers (somatic + autonomic)'

highlight:
Functional components of spinal nerves:
• GSA: General Somatic Afferent (pain, temp, touch from body)
• GSE: General Somatic Efferent (to skeletal muscle)
• GVA: General Visceral Afferent (from viscera)
• GVE: General Visceral Efferent (ANS to smooth muscle/glands)
mnemonic: 🧠 'Good Students Always Earn Good Grades Very Easily' = GSA, GSE, GVA, GVE

highlight:
Spinal nerve = Dorsal root (sensory/afferent) + Ventral root (motor/efferent)
Dorsal root ganglion contains cell bodies of sensory neurons.
Spinal nerve immediately divides into dorsal ramus (back) and ventral ramus (limbs, anterior trunk).
mnemonic: 🧠 'DAVE' = Dorsal = Afferent, Ventral = Efferent

highlight:
Sympathetic (Thoracolumbar T1-L2): fight or flight
• Pre-ganglionic SHORT, post-ganglionic LONG
Parasympathetic (Craniosacral CN III,VII,IX,X + S2-4): rest & digest
• Pre-ganglionic LONG, post-ganglionic SHORT
mnemonic: 🧠 'Sympathetic = Short pre, Parasympathetic = Short post' (opposite pre/post length)

highlight:
• Preganglionic (both SNS & PNS): Acetylcholine (nicotinic receptor)
• SNS postganglionic: Norepinephrine (adrenergic receptor) — EXCEPT sweat glands (ACh)
• PNS postganglionic: Acetylcholine (muscarinic receptor)
mnemonic: 🧠 'All Pre = ACh, SNS post = NE (except sweat = ACh), PNS post = ACh'

highlight:
• Dermatome: area of skin innervated by a SINGLE spinal nerve (sensory)
• Myotome: group of muscles innervated by a SINGLE spinal nerve (motor)
• Adjacent dermatomes overlap → need to damage 3 consecutive levels to lose complete sensation
mnemonic: 🧠 'Derm = skin, Myo = muscle, both = one spinal nerve'

highlight:
Arteries: thicker wall, more elastic & smooth muscle, maintain shape
Veins: thinner wall, larger lumen, VALVES (prevent backflow), collapse when empty
Capillaries: single endothelial cell layer + basement membrane (site of exchange)
mnemonic: 🧠 'Arteries = Away from heart = thick walls, Veins = toward heart = valVes'

highlight:
End artery: an artery with NO anastomosis (no collateral circulation)
→ Occlusion causes INFARCTION
Examples: central artery of retina, coronary arteries (functional end arteries), renal arteries
mnemonic: 🧠 'End artery = End of the line → Blockage = Death of tissue'

highlight:
Lymph drains from tissues → lymph capillaries → lymph vessels → lymph nodes → lymphatic trunks → thoracic duct (left side, drains ~75% of body) OR right lymphatic duct (drains right arm, right thorax, right head)
→ Both drain into venous system at junction of subclavian & internal jugular veins
mnemonic: 🧠 'Right duct = Right upper quadrant of body only; Thoracic duct = Everything else'

highlight:
Lymph nodes:
• Filter lymph (remove bacteria, cancer cells)
• Site of lymphocyte proliferation (immune response)
• Hilum: where artery enters and vein/efferent vessel exits
• Cortex: B cells (follicles); Paracortex: T cells; Medulla: macrophages
mnemonic: 🧠 'B cells in cortex, T cells deeper (Paracortex = T cells), Macrophages in Medulla'

highlight:
Serous membrane = parietal layer (lines cavity) + visceral layer (covers organ)
Cavities: pleural (lungs), pericardial (heart), peritoneal (abdomen)
Between layers: thin film of serous fluid (reduces friction)
mnemonic: 🧠 'PVF = Parietal lines the wall, Visceral covers the organ, Fluid between'

highlight:
Mucous membranes (mucosa) line body cavities OPEN to exterior:
• Respiratory, GI, urinary, reproductive tracts
• Components: epithelium + lamina propria + muscularis mucosae
• Goblet cells secrete mucus for protection and lubrication
mnemonic: 🧠 'Mucosa = open to outside world (respiratory, GI, GU tracts)'

highlight:
Simple reflex arc components:
1. Receptor
2. Afferent neuron (sensory)
3. Interneuron (in spinal cord)
4. Efferent neuron (motor)
5. Effector (muscle/gland)
Monosynaptic reflex: NO interneuron (e.g., patellar reflex)
mnemonic: 🧠 'RAIE+E' = Receptor, Afferent, Interneuron, Efferent, Effector

highlight:
UMN (Upper Motor Neuron — brain/cord):
→ Spasticity, hyperreflexia, + Babinski, no atrophy
LMN (Lower Motor Neuron — anterior horn/peripheral nerve):
→ Flaccidity, hyporeflexia, atrophy, fasciculations
mnemonic: 🧠 'UMN = Up = hyperreflexia, LMN = Low = loss of reflexes + atrophy'

highlight:
Somatic pain: well-localized, sharp, from body wall/muscles/joints
Visceral pain: poorly localized, crampy/dull, from internal organs
Referred pain: visceral pain felt at distant somatic site (e.g., cardiac pain → left arm; diaphragm irritation → shoulder tip)
mnemonic: 🧠 'Visceral = Vague (poorly localized), Somatic = Specific (well localized)'

highlight:
Anastomosis: connection between two vessels
→ Provides COLLATERAL CIRCULATION if one vessel is blocked
Types: arterial, venous, arteriovenous (AVA)
Clinically important: coronary collaterals, circle of Willis (cerebral), portal-systemic anastomoses
mnemonic: 🧠 'Anastomosis = Alternative route = insurance against blockage'

highlight:
Primary intention: clean wound edges, minimal scarring
Secondary intention: wound left open, granulation tissue fills gap, more scarring
Factors impairing healing: infection, poor blood supply, diabetes, malnutrition (especially Vitamin C deficiency), steroids
mnemonic: 🧠 'Primary = Perfect closure, Secondary = Scar-forming open wound'
